g1.label: 1. She ___ to school by bus every day.
g1.why: Third person singular in the present simple takes -s: she goes.

g2.label: 2. There ___ three books on the table.
g2.why: 'There are' for plurals; 'there is' is only for singular or uncountable nouns.

g3.label: 3. My birthday is ___ July.
g3.why: Months take 'in': in July. 'On' is for days, 'at' for clock times.

g4.label: 4. ___ you like coffee?
g4.why: Questions in the present simple use do/does; 'you' takes 'do'.

g6.label: 6. I ___ my keys yesterday.
g6.why: 'Lose' is irregular: the past form is 'lost', never 'losed'.

g7.label: 7. My brother is ___ than me.
g7.why: Short adjectives form the comparative with -er: tall → taller.

g8.label: 8. We ___ visit our grandparents next weekend.
g8.why: 'Going to' needs the verb 'be': we are going to visit.

g9.label: 9. There isn't ___ milk in the fridge.
g9.why: Negatives take 'any', not 'some': there isn't any milk.

g10.label: 10. Look! It ___.
g10.why: 'Look!' signals right now, so use the present continuous: is raining.

g11.label: 11. I have never ___ to Japan.
g11.why: The present perfect is have + past participle; the participle of 'be' is 'been'.

g12.label: 12. If I ___ rich, I would travel the world.
g12.why: Second conditional: if + past simple, and 'were' for all persons after 'if I'.

g13.label: 13. This house ___ in 1920.
g13.why: Past simple passive: was/were + past participle — was built.

g14.label: 14. I enjoy ___ books.
g14.why: 'Enjoy' is always followed by the gerund (-ing), never the infinitive.

g15.label: 15. She ___ here since 2019.
g15.why: 'Since' with a start point takes the present perfect: has lived.

g16.label: 16. When I arrived, the film ___ already ___.
g16.why: The earlier of two past actions takes the past perfect: had started.

g17.label: 17. If you had studied, you ___ the exam.
g17.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle.

g18.label: 18. He said he ___ the next day.

g19.label: 19. That's the man ___ dog bit me.
g19.why: Possession in a relative clause needs 'whose' — the man's dog.

g20.label: 20. I wish I ___ harder when I was at school.
g20.why: Wishes about the past take the past perfect: I wish I had studied.

g21.label: 21. Rarely ___ such a talented singer.
g21.why: After negative adverbs like 'rarely', subject and auxiliary invert: rarely have I heard.

g22.label: 22. ___ the report, she sent it to her manager.
g22.why: A perfect participle clause shows the first action was complete: having finished.

g23.label: 23. The teacher suggested that he ___ the essay again.
g23.why: After 'suggest that', use the base subjunctive — 'write', no -s.

g24.label: 24. ___ it not for your help, I would have failed.
g24.why: Formal inversion replaces 'if it were not for': were it not for.

g25.label: 25. Scarcely had I arrived ___ the phone rang.
g25.why: The pair is 'scarcely … when'; 'than' belongs with 'no sooner'.
